question: Match each data file format to the description that fits it best.
targetSlots: Plain text in which each line is one record and a character such as a comma separates the field values
Human-readable text that represents data as name/value pairs with nested objects and arrays
Row-based binary format in which records are serialized using a schema that is stored with the data
Text markup that encloses each data element in opening and closing tags
explanation:
- **Delimited text (CSV)** — The simplest tabular text format: one record per line, fields separated by a delimiter (usually a comma), often with a header row. Universally supported for data exchange.
- **JSON (JavaScript Object Notation)** — Human-readable text built from **name/value pairs**, with support for **nested objects and arrays**, which makes it the standard format for semi-structured data and web APIs.
- **Avro** — A **row-based binary** serialization format. Each Avro file carries the **schema** used to serialize its records, so readers can interpret the binary data; it is widely used in streaming and big-data ingestion pipelines where compact row-oriented records matter.
- **XML (eXtensible Markup Language)** — Text markup in which every element is wrapped in **opening and closing tags** (with optional attributes). Verbose compared with JSON, but still common in enterprise integrations.

A useful contrast for the exam: CSV and XML and JSON are human-readable text; Avro is binary and row-oriented (optimized for writing and transporting whole records), whereas columnar binary formats like Parquet are optimized for analytical reads of selected columns.
